1.title: Quick-Reference Recap and Decision Chooser
1.text: Welcome to Module eighteen: Quick-Reference Recap and Decision Chooser. This module covers quick-reference recap and decision chooser. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. One-page decision tables for each domain. The names, numbers and limits worth memorizing. The distractor patterns that make wrong answers attractive.

1.title: Case Check-In: Lumen Advisory
1.text: Our running case is Lumen Advisory. Lumen Advisory. The architect meets the topic of this module. Your job: decide, step by step, which design choice fits best.

1.title: Decision Chooser
1.text: Decision Chooser. The figure shows this: The decision chooser: for each recurring architect decision, ask the deciding question and pick the matching answer.

1.title: D1 Solution Design (17%) and D2 Models, Prompting, Context (13%)
1.text: D one Solution Design (seventeen percent) and D two Models, Prompting, Context (thirteen percent). Pattern. Deciding question: Are the steps known? Answer: Known: workflow; unpredictable: orchestrator-workers or agent; start simplest. Multi-agent? Deciding question: High value, parallel, beyond one context? Answer: Yes: orchestrator-worker; else workflow. Model tier. Deciding question: What is the binding constraint? Answer: Volume and latency: light; balanced: mid; hard reasoning: strong; prove with evals. Prompt content. Deciding question: Does it repeat? Answer: Static first, dynamic last, cache the prefix. Technique. Deciding question: Format or tone hard to describe? Answer: Few-shot; multi-step reasoning: chain-of-thought or effort. Context too big. Deciding question: What is bloating it? Answer: Prune, compact, isolate, external memory. Prompt reuse. Deciding question: Procedure or background? Answer: Skill (procedure), Project or knowledge (background), M C P (live data).

1.title: D3 Integration (19%)
1.text: D three Integration (nineteen percent). Too many tools. Deciding question: Does the role need them? Answer: Remove unneeded; then defer with tool search; code execution for data-heavy tools. Security gap. Deciding question: Who is acting and what may they do? Answer: Per-user identity and authorization in code; least privilege; secrets server-side. Integration. Deciding question: Reusable shared capability? Answer: M C P; simple owned call: A P I (application programming interface) or C L I (command-line interface); delegate to another agent: A to A. M C P auth. Deciding question: H T T P or S T D I O? Answer: H T T P: OAuth two point one, P K C E, audience check, no passthrough; S T D I O: environment. R A G or not. Deciding question: Corpus size and change? Answer: Under about two hundred thousand tokens: cached prompt; larger or filtered: R A G.

1.title: D3 Integration (19%), continued
1.text: D three Integration (nineteen percent), continued. Retrieval. Deciding question: Data shape? Answer: Prose: hybrid plus rerank, identifiers: keyword, tables: S Q L (Structured Query Language), code: search tools. Wrong answers after refresh. Deciding question: Where first? Answer: Retrieval and indexing. Latency versus accuracy. Deciding question: Client priority? Answer: Measure; stream, cache, route, batch; justify. Observability. Deciding question: Scale and privacy? Answer: Metrics for all, sampled redacted traces, quality sampling, cost attribution.

1.title: D4 Evaluation (16%), D5 Governance (14%), D6 Stakeholders (14%), D7 Productivity (7%)
1.text: D four Evaluation (sixteen percent), D five Governance (fourteen percent), D six Stakeholders (fourteen percent), D seven Productivity (seven percent). Define quality. Numeric criteria on a held-out dataset, several dimensions. Grading. Code (checkable), L L M (large language model) judge with rubric, different model, calibrated, human for calibration. Release a change. Offline eval, then A or B or canary, baseline comparison, rollback. Diagnose. Reproduce; find the layer; inspect what the model saw; one change. Optimize. Cost per successful task; reject savings that break gated metrics. Guardrails. Layers; assume the model can be wrong; hard controls in code; approvals for irreversible actions. Injection. Untrusted content as data; no instructions in tool results; screen outputs; red-team.

1.title: D4 Evaluation (16%), D5 Governance (14%), D6 Stakeholders (14%), D7 Productivity (7%), continued
1.text: D four Evaluation (sixteen percent), D five Governance (fourteen percent), D six Stakeholders (fourteen percent), D seven Productivity (seven percent), continued. Human oversight. Gate before irreversible; sample after reversible; queue by risk; meaningful review. H I P A A or Fed R A M P or G D P R. B A A and eligible features or authorized route (Gov Cloud or Vertex with Assured Workloads) or D P A, minimization, residency. Ethics. Subgroup tests, human decisions, disclosure, citations. Discovery. All stakeholders, real examples, measurable outcomes, constraints. S L A (service level agreement). Honest, measurable; quality as percent on a test set; fallbacks. Handoff. Versioned prompts, evals, runbooks, A D R s, owners. Team policy. Managed settings; commit Claude dot M D and shared settings; hooks and permissions deterministic. Exam tip: When two options both work, prefer the one that is simple, least-privileged, measured, cost-aware and compliant.

1.title: Names and Values to Know
1.text: Names and Values to Know. Exam. C C A R P; sixty-three items; one hundred twenty min; seven hundred twenty of one thousand; U S D one hundred seventy-five; valid twelve months. Domain weights. D three nineteen, D one seventeen, D four sixteen, D five fourteen, D six fourteen, D two thirteen, D seven seven. Tiers. Haiku fast and cheap, Sonnet balanced, Opus strong, Fable strongest. Context or output. one million tokens or one hundred twenty-eight thousand. Savings. Batch fifty percent off; cache reads ten percent of base input (five percent or two point five percent on some tiers). Cache. Static first; up to four breakpoints; five min or one hour; about five hundred twelve-token minimum. Agents versus chat tokens. Agents about four times; multi-agent about fifteen times.

1.title: Names and Values to Know, continued
1.text: Names and Values to Know, continued. Tool search. Use at ten plus tools or over ten thousand tokens; accuracy falls beyond thirty to fifty tools; keep three to five loaded. Contextual retrieval. fifty to one hundred token context; failure -thirty-five percent, -forty-nine percent, -sixty-seven percent with B M twenty-five and rerank; rerank one hundred fifty to twenty. No-R A G threshold. About two hundred thousand tokens. Eval start. About twenty cases. M C P auth. OAuth two point one for H T T P; four hundred one token, four hundred three insufficient scope. Z D R. No storage at rest; per org; no browser calls. H I P A A. B A A plus eligible features. Fed R A M P. Via Gov Cloud or Vertex with Assured Workloads; not the direct A P I. Covered Models. thirty-day retention.

1.title: Names and Values to Know, continued
1.text: Names and Values to Know, continued. Claude Code scopes. Managed greater than command line greater than project local greater than shared project greater than user. Model names, prices, platform authorizations and settings keys change; the principles behind them are what the questions test. Exam tip: Numbers matter most where they decide a design choice: about fifty-five thousand tokens of tool definitions, thirty to fifty tools, two hundred thousand tokens for the no-R A G threshold, fifteen times tokens for multi-agent.

1.title: Distractor Patterns
1.text: Distractor Patterns. Add logging or a confirmation instead of removing a tool. Why it is tempting: Feels safe. Why it fails: Compensating, not least privilege. A bigger model fixes it. Why it is tempting: Capability sounds like the cure. Why it fails: Does not fix retrieval, authorization or design. Always the largest or always the smallest. Why it is tempting: Simple rule. Why it fails: Ignores the eval. An agent for a fixed task. Why it is tempting: Modern. Why it fails: More cost and compounding errors. Truncate or shrink blindly. Why it is tempting: Cheap. Why it fails: Loses needed content or quality. Put everything in a vector store. Why it is tempting: One tool. Why it fails: Wrong for tables, identifiers, code.

1.title: Distractor Patterns, continued
1.text: Distractor Patterns, continued. Blame the model after a data refresh. Why it is tempting: Easy target. Why it fails: Check retrieval and indexing first. Stronger prompt wording. Why it is tempting: Quick. Why it fails: Not enforceable. Shared credential for convenience. Why it is tempting: Simple. Why it fails: No per-user permissions. Judge by a few examples. Why it is tempting: Fast. Why it fails: Needs datasets and controlled tests. Promise one hundred percent accuracy. Why it is tempting: Wins the deal. Why it fails: Quality is statistical. Assume any route is compliant. Why it is tempting: Convenient. Why it fails: Contract, features and platform matter. Log everything with full content. Why it is tempting: Debuggable. Why it fails: Cost and privacy risk. Skip handoff docs. Why it is tempting: Time pressure. Why it fails: System cannot be operated. Exam tip: A distractor often adds a control after the fact (logging, a confirmation, a bigger model); the correct answer removes the cause.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Design: Simplest pattern; workflows for known steps; multi-agent only when it pays. Models: Smallest that passes evals; route; pin. Context: Cache static prefix; prune, compact, isolate. Integration: Remove, then defer tools; identity in code; M C P versus A P I versus A to A; retrieval by data shape. Evaluation: Numeric criteria, datasets, mixed grading, A or B, diagnose by layer. Governance: Layered guardrails, human gates, right compliance route, ethics tests. Stakeholders: Discovery, honest trade-offs, S L A s, documentation, lifecycle. Teams: Managed settings, shared Claude dot M D, hooks, telemetry. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
